'''Francisco José García Torres''' (born 14 August 1999) is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left back|left-back]] for {{Spanish football updater|Real Betis}} club [[Real Betis]] and the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]].

==Club career==
===Real Madrid===
Born in [[Bolaños de Calatrava]], [[Ciudad Real]], [[Castilla–La Mancha]], García joined [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]'s [[La Fábrica (Real Madrid)|La Fábrica]] in 2013, from hometown side Bolaños CF.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elespanol.com/elbernabeu/cantera/20190128/fran-garcia-traspasa-fronteras-lateral-castilla-italia/371964030_0.html|title=Fran García traspasa fronteras: el lateral del Castilla del que hablan en Italia|trans-title=Fran García cross borders: the full back of Castilla that they talk about in Italy|publisher=El Español|language=es|date=28 January 2019|accessdate=13 September 2020}}</ref> On 1 February 2018, while still a junior, he renewed his contract until 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elespanol.com/elbernabeu/cantera/20180201/fran-garcia-renueva-real-madrid/281723239_0.html|title=Fran García renueva con el Real Madrid hasta 2022|trans-title=Fran García renews with Real Madrid until 2022|publisher=El Español|language=es|date=1 February 2018|accessdate=13 September 2020}}</ref>

Promoted to [[Real Madrid Castilla|the reserves]] ahead of the [[2018–19 Segunda División B|2018–19 season]], García made his senior debut on 9 September by playing the last 25 minutes of a 0–0 [[Segunda División B]] away draw against [[AD Unión Adarve]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/09/0-0-castilla-manage-a-hard-worked-draw-against-union-adarve|title=0–0: Castilla manage a hard-worked draw against Unión Adarve|publisher=Real Madrid|date=9 September 2018|accessdate=13 September 2020}}</ref> He made his first team debut on 6 December, coming on as a second-half [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Dani Carvajal]] in a 6–1 home routing of [[UD Melilla]], for [[2018–19 Copa del Rey|the season]]'s [[Copa del Rey]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2018/12/06/5c095d6fe2704e016c8b45f7.html|title=Fran Garcia and Alvaro Fidalgo handed senior debuts by Solari|publisher=Marca|date=6 December 2018|accessdate=6 September 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/12/fran-garcia-and-fidalgo-make-their-real-madrid-debuts|title=Fran García and Fidalgo make their Real Madrid debuts|publisher=Real Madrid|date=6 December 2018|accessdate=13 September 2020}}</ref>

García scored his first senior goal on 15 December 2019, netting his team's second in a 3–0 home win against [[Getafe CF B]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/12/15/3-0-castilla-run-riot-at-the-di-stefano|title=3–0: Castilla run riot at the Di Stéfano|publisher=Real Madrid|date=15 December 2019|accessdate=13 September 2020}}</ref>

===Rayo Vallecano===
On 1 September 2020, García was loaned to [[Segunda División]] club [[Rayo Vallecano]] for the [[2020–21 Segunda División|2020–21 campaign]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rayovallecano.es/noticia/fran-garcia-nuevo-jugador-del-rayo-vallecano|title=Fran García nuevo jugador del Rayo Vallecano|trans-title=Fran García new player of Rayo Vallecano|publisher=Rayo Vallecano|language=es|date=1 September 2020|accessdate=14 September 2020}}</ref> He made his professional debut thirteen days later, starting in a 1–0 away win against [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/segunda-division/mallorca-vs-rayo/cronica/2020/09/13/5f5e2f3e46163f9b648b4576.html|title=La intensidad del Rayo superó la calidad del Mallorca|trans-title=Rayo's intensity overcame Mallorca's quality|publisher=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=13 September 2020|accessdate=14 September 2020}}</ref> He immediately became a starter for [[Andoni Iraola]]'s side, but suffered a [[knee]] injury in November;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/rayo/2020/11/23/5fbbaf5cca4741661f8b45de.html|title=La peor noticia: ¡Fran García se pierde toda la temporada!|trans-title=The worst news: Fran García out for the whole season!|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=23 November 2020|accessdate=23 November 2020}}</ref> initially expected to miss the remainder of [[2020–21 Segunda División|the campaign]], he returned to play after 20 days.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/rayo/2020/12/06/5fccae1322601d4a268b45d8.html|title=El 'milagro' de Fran García|trans-title=The 'miracle' of Fran García|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=6 December 2020|accessdate=6 December 2020}}</ref>

On 13 July 2021, after helping in Rayo's promotion to [[La Liga]], García joined the club permanently on a four-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 July 2021|title=Fran García jugador del Rayo las próximas cuatro temporadas|trans-title=Fran García player of Rayo the following four seasons|url=http://www.rayovallecano.es/noticia/fran-garcia-jugador-del-rayo-las-proximas-cuatro-temporadas|access-date=14 July 2021|publisher=Rayo Vallecano|language=es}}</ref> He made his debut in the category on 15 August, starting in a 3–0 away loss to [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]]. In the [[2022–23 Rayo Vallecano season|2022–23 season]], his notable performance has attracted the attention of many clubs, including his childhood club, Real Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 December 2022 |title=Real Madrid consider bringing back Fran Garcia from Rayo Vallecano |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2022/12/26/63aa0f8dca47415a6a8b45fe.html |access-date=24 January 2023 |website=MARCA |language=en}}</ref>

===Return to Real Madrid===
On 9 June 2023, Real Madrid announced the re-signing of García until June 2027, after triggering the buy-back clause for a fee of €5m.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 June 2023 |title=Official Announcement: Fran García |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2023/06/09/official-announcement-fran-garcia |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230921121625/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2023/06/09/official-announcement-fran-garcia |archive-date=21 September 2023 |access-date=9 June 2023 |website=Real Madrid CF}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 June 2023 |title=Real Madrid signs Rayo Vallecano's defender Fran Garcia |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/soccer-real-madrid-signs-rayo-vallecanos-defender-fran-garcia-2023-06-09/ |access-date=10 June 2023 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> On 12 August 2023, he made his first appearance after the return, playing the full 90 minutes in a 2–0 away win over [[Athletic Bilbao]] in the league.<ref>{{cite web |date=12 August 2023 |title=Athletic Bilbao 0–2 Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham scores on his debut as Real win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66489759 |access-date=12 August 2023 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref> On 17 September, García delivered two assists in a La Liga fixture against [[Real Sociedad]], contributing to a 2–1 triumph for Real Madrid. For his standout performance, he was named the man of the match.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Two assists for Fran García: We have to be strong at home |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2023/09/17/two-assists-for-fran-garcia-we-have-to-be-strong-at-home |access-date=18 September 2023 |website= |publisher=Real Madrid CF |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=17 September 2023 |title=Real Madrid 2–1 Real Sociedad: Goals and highlights – LaLiga EA Sports 23/24 |url=https://www.marca.com/en/soccer/laliga/r-madrid-real-sociedad/2023/09/17/01_0101_20230917_186_188-live.html |access-date=18 September 2023 |website= |publisher=[[MARCA]] |language=en}}</ref> On 20 September, García made his [[UEFA Champions League]] debut in a [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]] match, coming on as a substitute for [[Nacho (footballer, born 1990)|Nacho]] against [[1. FC Union Berlin|Union Berlin]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=20 September 2023 |title=Real Madrid-Union Berlin: UEFA Champions League 2023/24 Group stage |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2039183--real-madrid-vs-union-berlin/ |access-date=20 September 2023 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}}</ref> On 11 May 2024, he scored his first league goal at the club in a 4–0 away win over [[Granada CF|Granada]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=Joseph |date=11 May 2024 |title=Real Madrid rests starters in 4–0 rout of relegated Granada with focus on Champions League final |url=https://apnews.com/article/real-madrid-granada-liga-5ef151ec8470e6c531f75e5497ef0c26 |access-date=11 May 2024 |publisher=[[AP News]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=11 May 2024 |title=Fran García: "Es una alegría inmensa marcar mi primer gol con el Real Madrid" |trans-title=Fran García: “I’m delighted to have scored my first goal for Real Madrid” |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/es/news/football/first-team/latest-news/fran-garcia-11-05-2024 |access-date=12 May 2024 |website= |publisher=Real Madrid CF |language=es}}</ref> On 5 July 2025, García scored the second goal for Real Madrid in a 3–2 victory over [[Borussia Dortmund]] in the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup knockout stage|FIFA Club World Cup quarter-finals]], securing their advancement to the semi-finals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Botte |first=Peter |date=5 July 2025 |title=Real Madrid beat Borussia Dortmund to set up star-studded Club World Cup semifinal |url=https://nypost.com/2025/07/05/sports/real-madrid-beat-borussia-dortmund-to-set-up-star-studded-club-world-cup-semifinal/ |access-date=5 July 2025 |publisher=[[New York Post]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=5 July 2025 |title=Real Madrid 3-2 Dortmund: FIFA Club World Cup 2025 |url=https://www.marca.com/en/soccer/fifa-club-world-cup/r-madrid-borussia-dortmund/2025/07/05/01_01130_20250705_186_157-live.html |access-date=5 July 2025 |publisher=MARCA |language=en}}</ref>

===Real Betis===
On 8 July 2026, García was transferred to fellow La Liga club [[Real Betis]], signing a four-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 July 2026 |title=Official Announcement: Fran García |url=https://en.realbetisbalompie.es/news/latest_news/official-announcement-fran-garcia-32510 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714193833/https://en.realbetisbalompie.es/news/latest_news/official-announcement-fran-garcia-32510 |archive-date=14 July 2026 |access-date=2026-08-09 |publisher=[[Real Betis Balompié]] |language=en-EN}}</ref>

==International career==
On 12 June 2023, García was called up to the senior [[Spain national football team|Spanish national team]] squad for the first time for the [[2023 UEFA Nations League Finals]], replacing [[Juan Bernat]]. He remained as an unused substitute during the two matches against [[Italy national football team|Italy]] and [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 June 2023 |title= Fran García replaces Juan Bernat in Spain squad |url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/fran-garcia-replaces-juan-bernat-in-spain-squad-37662677 |access-date=12 June 2023 |website=OneFootball |language=en}}</ref>

On 12 October 2023, García made his international debut for Spain during a [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying Group A|UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying match]] against [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 October 2023 |title=Bryan Zaragoza, Fran García and Oihan Sancet receive their commemorative badges, marking their debut for Spain |url=https://rfef.es/en/noticias/bryan-zaragoza-fran-garcia-and-oihan-sancet-receive-their-commemorative-badges-marking-their-debut-for-spain |access-date=16 October 2023 |website=Real Federación Española de Fútbol |language=en}}</ref> which Spain won 2–0.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 October 2023 |title=Spain wins 25th straight qualifier at home to keep Scotland from clinching spot in Euro 2024 |url=https://apnews.com/article/european-qualifying-roundup-spain-scotland-2c8c24d31dcba9b11e7a3eb855c6458c |access-date=16 October 2023 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>
